blind.B1: Yes. Aged male F344BN rats, 3 probiotic arms (CON, LP, LPA) x sedentary/treadmill exercise (12 wk, 5 d/wk), RNA-seq of 5 tissues (S2.2, S2.4.3, treatment_protocol_ch1). Exercise arms are CONEx, LPEx, LPAEx (CE, PE, AE in titles; activity=Exercise: 89 samples).
blind.B2: All other groups versus LPAEx, per tissue (PFC, hippocampus, colon, liver, TA muscle); n = 4-6 animals/group (S2.4.3.p1, S2.4.3.2.p1, TAB2/TAB3). The comparison that isolates exercise is LPAEx vs LPASed.
blind.B3: Each animal contributes one sample to each of the five tissues (animal number in the title, e.g. CS3 in PFC_/Hippo/L_/C_/M_), so repeated measures exist across tissues. Packet A lists no candidate key because the key is embedded in the title. Within one tissue each animal appears once, so a per-tissue model needs no blocking.
blind.B4: Per-tissue DESeq2 with the single-factor ~group design: 'we utilized the ~group design ... DEGs for all groups compared with LPAEx in each respective tissue group' (S2.4.3.2.p1).
blind.B5: 'false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.10 (Benjamini-Hochberg) and an absolute log2fold change (|LFC|) > 1.0' (S2.4.3.2.p1). Counts in TAB2 (PFC: 317, 203, 170, 14, 4) and TAB3 (liver: 112, 143, 73, 19, 258); muscle vs CONEx 15; hippocampus vs CONSed 19; the others 2-14 (S3.4).

checks.evidence: Exercise arms CONEx/LPEx/LPAEx exist; the case ran. The paper_aligned route follows S2.4.3.2.p1.

Groups from the title code match the activity and treatment fields. n is 6/group/tissue (liver LPEx 5), inside the paper's 4-6. Two mislabelled liver samples (L_AE7 is colon, L_PE4 is muscle) are excluded with a named reason (Spearman to tissue medians); the paper does not say which samples it dropped, and this is stated as a deviation. L_AE11 is kept in the primary run and dropped in a labelled sensitivity run.
All contrasts have treatment=LPAEx and control=the other group. The paper reports 'upregulated' as higher in LPAEx (FIG5).
Repeated animals exist only across tissues; the fit is per tissue, one sample per animal, so no blocking is needed (covariance gate: not_required).
~group per tissue as in S2.4.3.2.p1; one 6-level model per tissue with all pairwise contrasts taken from it. The two exercise-only contrasts (CONEx vs CONSed, LPEx vs LPSed) are labelled exploratory.
No batch, lane, or housing field in the metadata; sex is constant (male). The record says no batch variable is available.
STAR gene counts, 100% integers, median 1; pydeseq2 Wald in place of R DESeq2, recorded as a deviation. p-value histograms are not piled near 1 (frac p>0.9 about 0.16-0.21).

FDR<0.10 and |LFC|>1, exclusive, transcribed exactly. The flag 'other_rule_matches_paper' is for PFC vs CONSed only (paper 170; applied 59; padj<0.05 & |lfc|>0.585 gives 186). It does not generalise: PFC vs LPASed gives 581 under that rule against the paper's 317, and the applied rule gives 295. So there is no consistent alternative rule. The gap is noted in HANDBACK but not in the recorded discrepancy list.
checks.fix: Add PFC LPAEx vs CONSed (59 vs 170) to the recorded paper-data discrepancies with disposition executable_without_change.

checks.evidence: Pairs compare the same contrast (LPAEx vs X, same tissue, same rule). Most counts are close (295/317, 97/112, 71/73, 150/143). HANDBACK names the PFC vs CONSed shortfall, and the study gate's 'reproduced' wording is slightly generous for that one pair. HANDBACK also states that the liver LPAEx signal depends on L_AE11.
No stop or refusal. The sample exclusions are supported by tissue-identity correlations in the alignment gate.

human_items: Which of the paper's unreported sample exclusions applies is not stated; the exclusion of the two mislabelled liver samples is an inference that matches the paper's counts.
summary: 该案例按论文方法(每个组织单独拟合 ~group 的 DESeq2,各组对 LPAEx,FDR<0.10 且 |LFC|>1)执行,分组、方向、阈值、配对均无问题。两个肉眼标成肝脏但表达为结肠/肌肉的样本被排除并说明理由,另做了 L_AE11 的敏感性分析。仅 PFC 的 LPAEx vs CONSed(59 对 170)差距较大,建议补入已记录的差异清单。
